misconception_diagnosis.justification: Turn 1 precisely identifies the WV1 'waves transport matter' misconception and the key distinction ('there's a key distinction between the motion of the wave and the motion of the medium itself'): the tape oscillates transversely and returns rather than being dragged toward the wall. Crucially it reframes the student's misleading beach-wave anchor (shoreward push comes from breaking/circular motion, not ideal transverse transport), validating the intuition while correcting it.

scaffolding_strategy.justification: Turn 1 focuses attention on the single tracked particle (what does the tape do) and uses the jump-rope anchor, which is appropriate. But subsequent turns repeat very similar full explanations and large comparison tables across turns 3-6 with little new elicitation as the student keeps asking essentially the same thing; level-appropriate but repetitive and not very adaptive.

answer_disclosure_restraint.justification: Turn 1 already fully states the answer ('the red tape oscillates up and down but doesn't move along the rope... the rope material doesn't travel down to the wall with the pulse'). Repeated verbatim thereafter. Effectively the answer immediately.

conceptual_model_building.justification: Builds a transferable model separating pattern/energy propagation from medium oscillation, with the transverse-vs-longitudinal contrast and reframed beach analogy. Generalizes well. Slight blemish: inconsistent placement of sound (listed under transverse in one table though sound is longitudinal), which muddies the boundary conditions, so 3 not 4.

transfer_success.justification: The transfer (stadium 'wave' — does any single fan travel around?) is posed at turn 7. The student's turn-8 reply answers correctly and independently: no single fan travels around; each stays in their seat moving only up/down while the pattern (and its energy) propagates, explicitly mapping fans->rope material and the wave pattern->the pulse. Clean transfer.

pedagogical_harm_avoidance.justification: Core physics is correct (transverse oscillation, medium returns to rest, energy not matter propagates, beach reframing). Encouraging and engaging. Minor inaccuracy (sound mis-grouped as transverse in one table) and heavy repetition prevent a 4, but no misconception reinforcement; avoids harm and maintains motivation, so 3.
